lineage: The Hopfield network (Hopfield 1982): a recurrent associative memory where patterns are stored as attractors of an energy function; presented a corrupted pattern, the dynamics descend the energy landscape and recall the nearest stored memory
version: github.com/takyamamoto/Hopfield-Network master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)
dependencies: matplotlib (for the demo plots; a headless run skips them)
entry_points: train (Hebbian weight matrix from patterns); predict (async/sync update to an attractor)

example.command: Techne harness: store a few binary patterns, present a NOISE-corrupted one, iterate the dynamics, check it recalls the correct stored pattern
example.input: a corrupted version of a stored pattern
example.output: the recovered (denoised) stored pattern; energy decreasing

upstream_docs: Hopfield, Neural networks and physical systems with emergent collective computational abilities, 1982

human_capability_summary.built_to: store patterns as stable attractors and RECALL the nearest stored pattern from a noisy or partial cue by iterating recurrent dynamics that minimise an energy function
human_capability_summary.pressure: recall from corrupted/partial input, and a hard capacity limit (~0.14N patterns) beyond which memories interfere and recall fails
human_capability_summary.success_means: a corrupted cue converges to the correct stored pattern; the network denoises and completes

known_human_problem_solved: content-addressable (associative) memory with error correction by attractor dynamics
human_environmental_pressure: noisy/partial input, bounded storage capacity, spurious attractors
human_failure_condition: above capacity (or with correlated patterns) it converges to a spurious/wrong attractor -- recalls a memory that was never stored
behavioral_entry_point: raise the corruption level of the cue, or store MORE patterns than ~0.14N, and watch recall fail into spurious attractors

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run hopfield-takyamamoto
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: store patterns as stable attractors and RECALL the nearest stored pattern from a noisy or partial cue by iterating recurrent dynamics that minimise an energy function
